title: Strict-local generic points are defined over local etale trait neighbourhoods
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $D=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ a chosen strict henselization, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, and $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-sc-ring-strict-henselization, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V$ be a finite-type $K$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $v:\operatorname{Spec}F\to V$ be a $K$-morphism. There exist a discrete valuation ring $A$, ring maps $R\to A\to D$ whose composite is the chosen structural map, and a point $v_A:\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}A\to V$, such that $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale and of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $A\to D$ is injective, local and faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and $v_A$ pulls back to $v$ along $\operatorname{Frac}A\hookrightarrow F$ [def-pc-base-change]. Local means that the maximal ideal of $A$ maps into that of $D$. No henselian hypothesis on $R$, properness of $V$, or integral extension $R\to A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), morphisms at a finite stage, together with the defining pointed-etale colimit of strict henselization. Agent specialization: over a DVR one can refine a pointed etale neighbourhood to an affine local DVR neighbourhood by removing its other finitely many points over the closed point and its other normal components. The full local-refinement argument is recorded in report.md; the assertion is not claimed to be the literal statement of 01ZM.

proof.text: First identify the two strict-henselization conventions. Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-triples-presentation] to the given pointed-algebra colimit $D$. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and its closed point, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3) identifies this residue-triple diagram with the opposite of the affine pointed-neighbourhood diagram. Thus $D$ is the scheme strict henselization at the corresponding geometric point, compatibly with $R\to D$: both are colimits of that same diagram, so the mutually inverse comparison maps are forced by their coprojections. The base stalk is $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), since every element outside the maximal ideal of a local ring is already invertible. A DVR is Noetherian because each ideal has one generator. Hence [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] applies and shows that $D$ is a DVR and $R\to D$ is injective and local. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$; its image in $D$ is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0AP3 (lemma-henselization-dvr); comparison through algebra.tex Tag 04GW and etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX

proof.text: By the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose from a finite affine cover a chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset V$ containing the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$, where $C$ is generated over $K$ by $c_1,\ldots,c_n$. The inverse image of $W$ is the entire one-point scheme, so $v$ factors through $W$. Under the affine spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] it gives a $K$-algebra map $\varphi:C\to F$. Write $\varphi(c_j)=a_j/b_j$ with $a_j,b_j\in D$ and $b_j\ne0$. This includes $n=0$.

Use a small representative category of pointed etale $R$-algebras: it is filtered by [lem-sc-pointed-etale-small-filtered], and its colimit is $D$ by [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1), each of the finitely many $a_j,b_j$ has a representative at a stage. Repeated use of filteredness gives one stage $(B,\chi)$ and elements $\alpha_j,\beta_j\in B$ whose images under the structural coprojection $h:B\to D$ are $a_j,b_j$. If $n=0$, use nonemptiness to choose a stage. Compose $h$ with $D\to k_R^{\mathrm{sep}}$; this is $\chi$ by uniqueness of the colimit map. The map $D\to k_R^{\mathrm{sep}}$ kills $\mathfrak m_RD=\mathfrak m_D$ by [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal], and its kernel is proper because $1$ maps to $1$; its kernel is therefore exactly $\mathfrak m_D$. Consequently $\ker\chi=q=h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$. Thus $q$ lies over $\mathfrak m_R$, because the structural map of step 1 is local. In particular $B$ is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different); finite simultaneous representatives in the filtered colimit

proof.text: There are only two primes of $R$: $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m_R$. Indeed, $R$ is a local domain of dimension one by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], so any other prime would give the strict chain $(0)\subsetneq p\subsetneq\mathfrak m_R$. For each of these two base primes $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] makes $B\otimes_R\kappa(p)$ etale over the field $\kappa(p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] this fibre is a finite product of fields and therefore has finitely many primes. The fibre-ring description [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and the localization spectrum correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] identify its primes with the primes of $B$ contracting to $p$: first invert $R\setminus p$, then quotient by $p$; prime ideals of a quotient are exactly preimages of primes containing the quotient ideal. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is finite.

Set $A=B_q$. It is canonically the stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at $q$, with its actual map from $R$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c). The point $q$ lies over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, so [lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk] shows that $A$ is a domain DVR, $R\to A$ is injective, and $\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$. Since $h(s)\notin\mathfrak m_D$ for every $s\notin q$, the formula $h_q(b/s)=h(b)h(s)^{-1}$ defines a map $h_q:A\to D$ extending $h$. Its inverse image of $\mathfrak m_D$ is $qA$, by the same formula. Hence $h_q$ is local and its composite with $R\to A$ is the prescribed $R\to D$.

source.place: Tag 0AP2 (lemma-Dedekind-etale-extension), closed-fibre local-ring case; schemes.tex Tag 01HV

proof.text: We now show that this particular prime localization is principal. For each of the finitely many primes $P\subset B$ not contained in $q$, choose $s_P\in P\setminus q$ and put $f=\prod_Ps_P$ (empty product $1$). Then $f\notin q$. A prime containing no power of $f$ cannot be one of those $P$, hence is contained in $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], every prime of $B_f$ is therefore contained in $qB_f$, and $qB_f$ itself is prime. Thus $B_f$ is local with maximal ideal $qB_f$. Every $s\in B\setminus q$ has invertible image in $B_f$. The universal properties now give inverse $B$-algebra maps $B_f\rightleftarrows B_q$: both composites fix every fraction. We obtain $A=B_q\cong B_f$. This explicitly isolates the local neighbourhood; it does not assume that an arbitrary prime localization of a finitely presented algebra is finitely presented.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization](2) to $R\to B$ and $f$. It shows that $\operatorname{Spec}B_f\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale, hence the identified morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale. Part (1), applied to $R\to A$, also supplies finite presentation. For completeness the scheme morphism is of finite presentation in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]: etaleness supplies local finite presentation, and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has two points by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one]. The preimage of any affine open is finite, hence quasi-compact. The diagonal also has this finite scheme as its domain, so its affine-open preimages are finite and quasi-compact as well. Thus the morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

The map $h_q:A\to D$ is injective. Its kernel is prime since $D$ is a domain. A local domain DVR has just the primes $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m_A$, by the same dimension-one chain argument used in step 4, using [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] for $A$. But $h_q(\pi)$ is the nonzero image of $\pi$ from step 1, whereas $\pi\in\mathfrak m_A$. Thus the kernel cannot be $\mathfrak m_A$ and must be zero. This also proves that each $\beta_j$ has nonzero image in $A$, since its image $b_j$ in $D$ is nonzero.

As $A\hookrightarrow D$ is an injection of domains, $D$ is torsion free over $A$: if $0\ne a\in A$ and $h_q(a)d=0$, the domain property of $D$ forces $d=0$. A DVR is a principal ideal domain [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $D$ flat over $A$. The map is local between local rings by step 5. Therefore [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] makes it faithfully flat.

Put $L=\operatorname{Frac}A$. The injections $R\hookrightarrow A$ and $A\hookrightarrow D\hookrightarrow F$ extend uniquely to $K\hookrightarrow L\hookrightarrow F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift], compatibly with the given map $K\to F$. In $L$ set $x_j=\alpha_j/\beta_j$, using the images in $A$. Their images in $F$ are $\varphi(c_j)$. Let $I$ be the kernel of the surjection $K[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to C$ defined by the chosen generators. For every $P\in I$, the image of $P(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ in $F$ is $P(\varphi(c_1),\ldots,\varphi(c_n))=0$. Since $L\hookrightarrow F$ is injective, $P(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=0$ in $L$. Thus evaluation factors through $C$ and defines a $K$-algebra map $\varphi_A:C\to L$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this gives $v_A:\operatorname{Spec}L\to W\subset V$. After pullback to $F$, its coordinate map agrees with $\varphi$ on $K$ and all generators, hence on $C$; therefore its pullback is exactly $v$. Together with steps 5, 7, 8 and 9, these are all the required clauses.

split_report.summary: Proved the stated local finite-presentation approximation in ten explicit steps using existing DAG nodes only. Lift finitely many numerators and denominators to a pointed etale stage; its spectrum is finite because the base trait has two points and both etale fibres are finite. Isolate the marked prime by one principal localization, identify its stalk DVR, prove the local map into the strict henselization injective and faithfully flat, and descend all coordinate relations using the embedding of fraction fields. The statement is unchanged. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves.

The statement is true; tested on Z_(p) with x^2-u (u a square unit) and x^2-p (vacuous). All steps hold with the cited statements. Step 1: the triples presentation plus etale-local-ring-triples(3) identify D with the scheme strict henselization (Omega = algebraic closure of K, whose separable part is K); the affine-stalk lemma gives O_{Y,y}=R; the DVR is Noetherian, so strict-henselization-dvr shows D is a DVR and R->D is injective and local. Step 3: the stage comes from the small filtered representative category and the elementwise colimit lemma; q = ker chi = h^{-1}(m_D) via m_R D = m_D. Step 4: Spec B is finite from the two primes of R and the etale fibres being finite products of fields, using the fibre-ring/localization correspondence. Step 5: etale-trait-stalk at q gives the DVR; h_q is local. Step 6: one finite product f gives B_q = B_f (elementary, correct). Step 7: etale and finite presentation, including qc/qs in the 01TP sense. Steps 8-9: injectivity, then PID torsion-free => flat, then local flat => faithfully flat. Step 10: unique fraction-field lifts and the coordinate relations descend by injectivity of L->F. Edge cases checked: n=0, V empty, zero fibres, f=1, imperfect residue fields.
